clue.text: Flasher shocking South Leigh

indicators.note: something shocking is in a terrible state, so the letters of the two words are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A man exposing himself has caused a scandal in the town of Leigh.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flasher' suggests an indecent exposer, but it is a building whose lamp flashes; 'shocking' is the anagram signal applied to SOUTH and LEIGH together.
explanation.definitionFit: A coastal tower warns ships by sending out regular flashes of light, so it is literally a flasher.

clue.text: Spread in papers supporting City

indicators.note: in a down clue a piece that supports another sits beneath it, so the papers come after the city

parts.note: LA, Los Angeles, is the standard crossword city
ID stands for identity papers

explanation.surface: Something has spread through the newspapers backing a city.
explanation.definitionFit: Spread as in a table set out or a carpet put down: past tense of lay, meaning placed out flat.

clue.text: Goalpost periodically breaks

indicators.note: periodically means at regular intervals, so every other letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: A goalpost keeps snapping from time to time.
explanation.definitionFit: Breaks as in openings or intervals, spaces between things, are synonyms of holes in a fence or pauses.

clue.text: Critical time in record centre

definitions.meaning: a decisive moment when things change direction
the spindle hole of a vinyl disc is the spot it spins about

explanation.surface: A decisive moment arrives in the middle of the gramophone disc.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is playful: the middle of a gramophone record is literally the spot about which it revolves.
explanation.definitionFit: A moment of crisis where events change course is a common idiom; the record's spindle spot is the literal sense.

clue.text: It may appear in bars of musical work as prelude to movement

indicators.note: a prelude comes before, so the musical work is placed in front of the movement

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a numbered musical work
a tic is an involuntary twitching movement

explanation.surface: A motif turns up in the bars of a composition, introducing its next movement.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'bars' are pubs, not musical measures: an Optic is the British device fixed to an upside-down spirit bottle that pours a measured shot.
explanation.definitionFit: A spirit-measure dispenser mounted behind the counter is a common fixture in British pubs.

clue.text: Noticed something happening internally at this age

indicators.note: internally means on the inside, so one piece is placed within the other

parts.note: noticed means seen
an event is something that happens

explanation.surface: Someone spotted an inner change happening at a certain stage of life.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase refers to a number of years old, here the last but two of the teens.

clue.text: One used to strike for green card

definitions.text: One used to strike for green
definitions.meaning: a golfer's implement for hitting the ball towards the putting surface
a playing card from the suit marked with black trefoils

explanation.walkthrough: 'green card' looks like the US residence permit, but the clue splits after 'green' (a golf green).
explanation.definitionFit: A golfer's stick for hitting the ball, and a playing card of the trefoil suit, share this word.

clue.text: Features of ill-meant boring punishment at school

indicators.note: boring means drilling into, so the rearranged letters go inside the punishment

parts.note: lines are sentences a pupil is made to write out repeatedly as a punishment

indicators.note: ill means badly, so the letters of the following word are put wrongly in a new order

explanation.surface: A malicious, tedious school punishment has its own characteristics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ill-meant' reads as one hyphenated adjective, but it splits: 'ill' is the anagram signal for the word after it, and 'boring' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means the distinctive lines or contours of a face, hence its features.

clue.text: Pungency of beer associated with head?

indicators.note: associated with means joined to, so the two pieces sit side by side

parts.note: bitter is a British style of hoppy draught beer
a ness is a headland, as in Loch Ness or Sheerness

explanation.surface: Is the sharpness of a pint linked to its frothy top?
explanation.walkthrough: The 'head' looks like froth on the beer; it is a promontory.
explanation.definitionFit: Pungency is a sharp, acrid taste, the quality of something tart or sour.

clue.text: Don't say it's obligatory

definitions.meaning: an example of a command form of a verb, the grammatical mood of orders

explanation.walkthrough: 'Don't say' reads as a hushed request, but it is itself an instance of the grammatical mood for commands.
explanation.definitionFit: The command mood in grammar, and something urgent and compulsory, share this word.

clue.text: One in flight from warring nations

indicators.note: from here means taken out of the letters of the following words, which conceal the answer

explanation.surface: Someone flees from countries at war.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One in flight' suggests a refugee; it is a flying insect.
explanation.definitionFit: A small two-winged fly is a creature that spends time airborne.

clue.text: Standard of programme notes at Symphony Hall?

definitions.text: Standard of programme notes at Symphony Hall?

parts.words: Standard of programme notes at Symphony Hall?
parts.note: reads as the quality of a concert brochure, but means the fixed tuning standard for the notes an orchestra plays

explanation.surface: How good are the printed programme notes at a concert venue?
explanation.definitionFit: The agreed reference tuning to which orchestral instruments are set is a standard for the notes in a programme.

clue.text: Feeling low, listening to CD after midnight

parts.note: while you are listening, the disc is on
after midnight it is so late

explanation.surface: Someone feels depressed, playing an album in the small hours.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling low means downcast and unhappy, the sense of the answer.

clue.text: Dangerous place to expose tip

parts.note: to flash is to expose briefly
a point is a tip or end

explanation.surface: A risky spot to reveal the end of something.
explanation.definitionFit: A place where trouble or violence is likely to erupt is a common sense of the word.

clue.text: Injustice displayed by brunette?

definitions.meaning: unjust treatment, a lack of equity
a dark-haired person shows the quality of not being blonde

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense splits the word as UN-FAIR-NESS: being not fair-haired, as a brunette is.
explanation.definitionFit: Lack of justice is one sense; a dark-haired person's not being blonde is the playful second.

clue.text: Old High German, Latin and French accent

parts.note: the grave is a French accent sloping down to the right, as in è

explanation.surface: Old High German, Latin and French accents sound like a philology lesson.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old High German' looks like the language but is a historical German nobleman.
explanation.definitionFit: A medieval German count with territorial jurisdiction was an old, high-ranking German.

clue.text: Idiot you texted operated cellphone lacking core security

parts.note: an ass is a fool
U is the text-message spelling of you
ran means operated, as a business

indicators.note: without its core means only the first and last letters of the word remain

explanation.surface: A fool who texted you ran a broken phone, lacking security.
explanation.definitionFit: Assurance is a guarantee or certainty, and insurance-style cover is a form of security.

clue.text: Completely knock barnacle off bar

indicators.note: knocking something about jumbles it, so the remaining letters are rearranged
off means taken away, so the letters of the bar are removed from the barnacle

explanation.surface: Scrape a barnacle right off a bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' strips BAR from BARNACLE, leaving NACLE, and 'knock' rearranges it.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adverb it means totally, as in 'clean forgot' or 'clean out of ideas'.

clue.text: Item worn cycling has approval in review

indicators.note: cycling means rotating, so a letter moves from one end of the word to the other
a review looks back, so the approval is read backwards

parts.note: OK means approval

explanation.surface: A garment for cycling gets the thumbs-up in a magazine review.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall military cap with a peak and plume is a piece of headgear, something worn.

clue.text: Misses could make assertion

indicators.note: could make means its letters could be rearranged to form something new

explanation.surface: Failures might lead someone to make a claim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Misses' suggests failures; it means young unmarried women.
explanation.definitionFit: Spanish young unmarried women, addressed as miss in English.

clue.text: Transshipper working in more than one business

indicators.note: working means operating differently, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A cargo shipper is employed by several companies.
explanation.definitionFit: Firms owned jointly by associates are businesses, and the plural matches 'more than one'.

clue.text: Game on board requiring woman to chase husband

indicators.note: to chase is to follow behind, so the woman comes after the husband

parts.note: Alma is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A board game where a wife has to run after her husband.
explanation.definitionFit: A Victorian strategy game of hopping pieces across a squared board, like Chinese chequers.

clue.text: Desire purification — but not at first

indicators.note: but not at first means without its first letter, so the opening letter is dropped

parts.note: a purge is a cleansing or purification

explanation.surface: Someone wants to be cleansed, though not at the outset.
explanation.definitionFit: A strong impulse or longing is a desire, the noun sense.

clue.text: Plain paper covering almost everything up

indicators.note: covering means wrapped round, so the paper goes outside the other piece

parts.note: FT is the Financial Times, a British newspaper

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters are read from bottom to top, backwards
almost means not quite complete, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: all means everything

explanation.surface: A plain sheet of paper is wrapped round almost everything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses only because this is a down clue, where the letters are read from the bottom; the shortened 'everything' is turned before 'covering' puts it inside the paper.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain land is level land without hills, an expanse of flat ground.

clue.text: Independent clergyman retired somewhere in South Bucks

indicators.note: retired means drawn back, so the clergyman's title is reversed

parts.note: Rev is short for Reverend, a clergyman

explanation.surface: An independent vicar has retired to a spot in southern Buckinghamshire.
explanation.walkthrough: Bucks is Buckinghamshire, a county west of London; the answer is a village there near Slough.
explanation.definitionFit: The village lies in the southern part of Buckinghamshire, so it is a place in that district.

clue.text: One-sided police lie naturally, but not extremely libellously

indicators.note: to police is to control and put in order, so the letters are rearranged
but not means except, so letters are taken away from the word
extremely means at the extremes, so the first and last letters are taken

explanation.surface: A biased police force lies as a matter of course, though not quite libellously.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely libellously' gives LY, which 'but not' removes from NATURALLY; 'police' then rearranges LIE plus NATURAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A decision taken by one party without the agreement of the other is lopsided, done by one side only.

clue.text: Volunteers risked having cover blown twice in assignment

parts.note: the TA, Territorial Army, was Britain's volunteer reserve force

indicators.note: having its cover blown means losing its outer letters, done twice so two letters go from each end

explanation.surface: Volunteer spies risked having their cover blown repeatedly on a mission.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having cover blown twice' strips RISKED to ISKE and then to SK.
explanation.definitionFit: A piece of work someone is given to do is an assignment or job.

clue.text: Unit of separation

definitions.meaning: a group of troops sent away from the main body for a special job
the state of being apart or aloof

explanation.definitionFit: A military group posted apart, and the condition of being cut off or aloof, share this word.
